capitalRatios.title: Capital adequacy ratios
capitalRatios.content:
CET1 ratio is Common Equity Tier 1 capital over risk-weighted assets, the strictest regulatory capital measure. The Basel total capital ratio adds Tier 2 (subordinated debt-like) capital on top and is what the Brazilian Central Bank's minimum requirement is actually set against.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: both ratios compressed from the mid-teens in FY2019-2021 toward 10-11% by FY2024-FY2025 -- still above regulatory minimums, but a narrower buffer than the bank carried pre-pandemic, worth watching alongside credit quality.

What to watch:

  • Basel ratio staying comfortably above the ~10.5% regulatory minimum (CET1 + buffers)
  • A widening gap between Basel and CET1 would mean more reliance on Tier 2 instruments

nplRatio.title: 90-day non-performing loan ratio
nplRatio.content:
The share of the loan book more than 90 days overdue -- the standard credit-quality indicator banks and regulators use to gauge asset-quality deterioration before it shows up in writeoffs.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: only disclosed quarterly from Q3 2025; it has drifted from 4.1% to 4.3% over the four quarters shown, a gradual rise worth tracking against the credit impairment charge line.

What to watch:

  • NPL ratio rising faster than the credit impairment charge, which would mean provisioning is lagging the deterioration
  • Divergence from peer Brazilian banks' NPL trends

expandedLoan.title: Expanded loan portfolio
expandedLoan.content:
Bradesco's own broader loan-book measure, which adds items such as guarantees, letters of credit and some securities activities to the on-balance-sheet loan book reported as NetLoansAndAdvances.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: only disclosed quarterly from Q3 2025; it grew from R$1.03tn to R$1.14tn over the four quarters shown, a faster pace than NetLoansAndAdvances alone would suggest.

What to watch:

  • Growth here outpacing NetLoansAndAdvances, meaning off-balance-sheet exposure is growing
  • Consistency with the deposit growth funding it

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Banco Bradesco S.A.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: Sanity check flagged implied P/E 1.6x (vs a 10yr average of 0.4x) and P/B 0.21x (vs a 10yr max of 0.10x). Investigation traced this to a BRL/USD currency-direction bug in the sanity checker's own historical-multiple calculation (scripts/sanity_check.py), not a defect in the valuation: it converts the USD ADR price the wrong way before comparing against BRL financials, understating every historical multiple by roughly the square of the FX rate. No change was made to the DCF model. Recomputed by hand and denominated consistently in BRL, the base case implies about 7.3x trailing recurring earnings and 1.1x book value -- both inside Bradesco's normal historical range (see implied_multiples_after_fix) -- so the valuation itself is not the problem; the checker's currency handling is. Fixing that checker is a separate, cross-ticker change out of scope for this run.
